title: Henri IV to Andre Hurault de Maisse, ambassador at Venice, 3 and 7 November 1592, in Maisse's Cipher (1592) (BnF fr. 16093 ff. 370, 373)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 16093 f. 370 (ark btv1b90074656, canvas 419; old Harlay ms. 1024 piece 224)

plaintext.source: Contemporary clerk's copy, fully in clear, BnF NAF 6984 (fonds Brienne 13) fol. 102v, ark btv1b100904592; located through the Harlay piece number in Berger de Xivrey, Lettres missives t. III

transcription.source: openapi.bnf.fr IIIF, views 419 (f. 370r, right page) and 420 (f. 370v, left page) at native 7029/6901 px
transcription.notes: Whole cipher passage transcribed 23 Oct 2026 (r2f): 31 recto lines and 32 verso lines; the right ends of verso lines run into the binding gutter and a few groups per line are not visible there; 42 groups marked uncertain. ct370.txt keeps the earlier 80-group opening.

transcription.source: not transcribed; read from the clear copy

system.summary: Maisse's Cipher (1592): a simple substitution on a 22-letter alphabet in figures 1-22, with doubled-letter signs (66, 67, 68, 72, 73), a second sign (omega) for d and a sparse nomenclator above the band.

diacritics.note: Overbars on the leaf mark ordinary scribal abbreviation in the plaintext spelling (l[ett]res, occa[si]on), not cipher values; separating dots divide figures.

system.doubled_letters: special sign (ff, mm, nn, ss, uu)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstruction from the sibling leaves of the same volume (henryiv_Maisse1.png, from f. 317), used; Savasse (1997) reconstructed it independently from the Manuscrit Revol
system.notes: Key: a=7 b=8 c=9 d=10 e=11 f=1 g=2 h=3 i=4 l=5 m=6 n=12 o=13 p=14 q=15 r=16 s=17 u=19 x=20 y=21 z=22; ff=66 mm=67 nn=68 ss=72 uu=73. An omega-shaped sign on f. 370 is a second sign for d and is absent from Tomokiyo's table. ff. 406/410 use a different cipher (maisse1593).

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's key for Maisse's Cipher (1592), published as an image on cryptiana and reconstructed from sibling leaves; no reading of ff. 370/373 published; he lists them as undeciphered (no contemporary decipherment, not unsolved), so he may have read them; contemporary clear copies of both letters in Brienne 13 (NAF 6984), unprinted

conditions.human_role: Project-level only: the target was taken from the repository's catalogue and worked by the model in Claude Code; no target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: segmentation and reading aids (seg.py, seg2.py, boxes.py, zoom.py, montage.py)
glyph clustering (glyphs.py, digits.py, cluster.py), left unfinished
blind known-plaintext alignment with a shuffled-cipher control (align.py, align2.py, control.py)

solution.what: Tomokiyo's Henri IV page re-read as HTML rather than as the text dump in research/gallica_sweep/src: the four leaves fall in two different cipher sections, each with siblings in the same volume, so the entry's class B and 'no sibling found' were both wrong.
fr. 16093 resolved to ark btv1b90074656 by Gallica SRU and the folio-to-canvas offsets calibrated by reading folio numbers off the leaves.
The opening of f. 370 transcribed group by group (80 groups) from the native-resolution scan.

Blind frequency analysis of the transcription: 94% of groups in a contiguous band 1-22, commonest value 14.5%, sparse values above the band - a simple substitution with a small nomenclator, not the assumed homophonic system.

Blind known-plaintext alignment of the transcription against the Brienne clear text placed 12 groups against a shuffled-cipher control of mean 8.2 and p95 11 - at the noise floor, because the transcription mis-split 9 7 as 97 and homophony was wrongly assumed.

The old Harlay piece numbers on the leaves (224, 226 for ff. 370, 373; 247, 251 for the 1593 leaves) matched to Berger de Xivrey's citations, which give a clear copy in fonds Brienne 13 = NAF 6984 for each; the copies located on the images by heading and preamble.
Tomokiyo's key images fetched from his page (invisible in a text dump); the cipher 1 key (henryiv_Maisse1.png) transcribed to key1.tsv.
The key applied to the 80 transcribed groups of f. 370 and the result normalised against Brienne 13 fol. 102v: 81 of 81 characters identical.
ff. 370 and 373 read from the Brienne clear copies (fol. 102v, 104v).

Novelty re-examined after Lasry's note on 'undeciphered'. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The page no longer says Tomokiyo 'never applied' his keys; the claim is a published reading only.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from maisse1592, which had joined ff. 370/373 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592) with ff. 406/410 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592-93, the Breves cipher). This profile keeps ff. 370 and 373 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): f. 370: ct370.txt and the decode.py output with the Brienne comparison (texts/f370_decryption.md), opening only; f. 373 has no transcription or decryption in the repository, linked to the Gallica images of the leaf and of the Brienne 13 clear copy.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): texts/f370_decryption.md read: the 80-group opening reads and matches the Brienne copy (reviewed A), but the rest of f. 370 and all of f. 373 are not transcribed, and neither clear copy is in the repository. f. 373 relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> read in part; fraction_read 1.0 -> about 0.06 (estimated).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b29): f. 373r-v fetched at full size (Gallica btv1b90074656 views 422-423, openapi IIIF) and the contemporary clear copy Brienne 13 fol. 104r foot-106v top (btv1b100904592 views 109-112) transcribed in full for the first time (texts/f373_brienne_copy.txt). The copy omits the close and a six-line clear postscript (Joyeuse's defeat at Villemur), read from the original with two lines partly illegible.

The copy checked against the f. 373 figures with key1.tsv at five places (dautant que cela me peut beaucoup ayder a me resouldre; faict pour faire continuer / que les ennemis pourroient faire contre moy; publie par dela du; plus dadvancement a mes affai[res]; de tant linsolence et audace de cet ennemy; dela a mondict service): no disagreement. The name the copy writes Vivac not settled on the figures. Reading texts/f373_reading.md: 0.924 clean sentences (85/92), explicit holes 0.978; state decoded, not read -> read (grade A).

v3 verification: f. 370 had only its 81-letter opening read (0.545 on the decryption file). The cipher passage's contemporary clear copy, Brienne 13 fol. 102v-103v (pièce 224), transcribed from openapi.bnf.fr views 108-109; the passage's end fixed on f. 370v (view 420), where the original returns to clear with 'depuis le partement'. texts/f370_reading.md: 0.979 explicit-hole, 0.936 plain. Figures beyond the opening not aligned.

r2f: the whole cipher passage of f. 370 transcribed group by group from openapi.bnf.fr views 419 (f. 370r) and 420 (f. 370v) at native size, in line bands and zooms: 31 recto and 32 verso lines, 2,293 figure groups measured (texts/f370_figures.txt), 42 marked uncertain; verso line ends run into the binding gutter (30 lines lose a group or more).

r2f: the figures decoded with Tomokiyo's key and aligned with the Brienne 13 fol. 102v-103v copy by edit distance (research/reading_audit/r2f_align370.py; abbreviation bars, code groups and gutter marks may absorb copy letters): the alignment spans the whole copy, so the copy is this letter; 2,255 of 2,310 covered copy letters agree (97.6%), 45 substituted, 10 missing, 26 extra figure letters; by word 491 of 531 visible words agree. Differences classed in texts/f370_figures_vs_copy.md: 6 wording differences and about 20 spellings where the reading now follows the figures, about 20 enciphering slips where it keeps the copy (e.g. sois parsz sisost for soit passé sitost), 147 letters in the gutter.

r2f key rebuild from the alignment: 71 = rr (arriuer, pourront, angleterre), 73 = tt (attendant; key1.tsv had 73 = uu from Tomokiyo's table, where 73 is unlabelled under u; 71 rr, 72 ss, 73 tt keep the alphabetical order of the doubles 66 ff, 67 mm, 68 nn), codes 23 = pape (twice), 24 = Roy d'Espagne (Savasse's 1590 value), 48 = ambassadeur, 49 = guerre; Savasse's 23 = votre Majesté / le roi does not hold here. 90 (once, line end) unidentified. key1.tsv extended.

r2f: texts/f370_reading.md rebuilt to follow the figures where they differ from the copy (vouldriez, ou restraigniez, concernans, traictees, lesquelz, si c'estoit, period spellings), keeping the copy over enciphering slips; the copy kept unchanged as texts/f370_brienne_copy.txt; English texts/f370_en.md written. v2_score 0.979 plain (46/47), 1.0 explicit holes.

r2f: f. 373 words left open checked on view 422: the copy's [?Vivac] is Verac in the figures (19 11 16 7 9, no et before sa), [?chauvez] is charmez (9 3 7 16 6 11 22), [?sainement] confirmed (17 7 4 12 11 6 11 12 18). f373_reading.md 0.946 plain, 0.967 explicit holes.

r2f escalation: siblings - neighbouring leaves ff. 367-369 and 371-372 (views 416-418, 420-421) looked at: clear despatches and the clear close of f. 370, no duplicate of f. 370 by a second route that could fill the gutter; known keys - Tomokiyo's 1592 key fits (97.6%), his 1592-1593 key (maisse1593) does not apply (no letter-shaped signs on ff. 370/373), Savasse's codes from Maisse's 1590 letters agree on 24 and not on 23; not available here: Savasse 1997.

r2l: f. 373r-v fetched at full size from openapi.bnf.fr IIIF (views 422-423, 6959 x 6145 and 6823 x 6171), deskewed (2.95 and 1.3 degrees), rows found by ink profile (r2l_lines373.py), every line cut in four quarters at 1.35x (r2l_q373.py) and read figure by figure against the Brienne copy enciphered with key1.tsv (r2l_pred373.py), recording the figures where they differ; texts/f373_figures.txt, 3,958 groups in 66 lines (r03-r53, v01-v15), 36 doubtful, 3 struck. The recto has 51 cipher lines (b29 counted about 42), the verso 15 (b29: 11).

r2l: figures aligned letter by letter with the Brienne 13 copy (research/reading_audit/r2l_align373.py, copy of r2f_align370.py) -> texts/f373_figures_vs_copy.md: 3,972 of 4,062 copy letters agree (97.8%), 29 substituted, 48 missing, 13 in code 24. Differences in wording followed in the reading (pouvez tascher de, fort bon, asseurer ce faisant, Verac sa, combien qui, par faulte d'estre, le moien que j'ay); v2_score 0.913 plain, 0.957 explicit holes. fraction_read measured 0.999; class read in part -> read.

Independent blind re-transcription of f. 373 (sr): 6 lines drawn with random.seed(373) from recto ll. 3-53 + verso ll. 1-15 (r07, r15, r17, r18, r48, v13) read group by group from Gallica btv1b90074656 views 422-423 (full size), decoded with key1.tsv, without opening texts/f373_figures.txt or the Brienne copy; then compared group by group with f373_figures.txt (texts/f373_sr_blind.txt): 342 of 366 groups agree (94.1% Dice); the differences re-checked on the image fall on the blind reader's side.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py, key1.tsv + figures only): 97.3% (f. 370) and 99.7% (f. 373) of decoded letters align with the readings. Blind re-reading of five f. 370 lines drawn with random.seed(370) (r30, v09, v10, v25, v29; 182 groups) from the Gallica images: 177 agree with f370_figures.txt (Dice 97.3%). v29 figure is 8 (encipherer's slip for 9); the code for pape looks like 25, not 23 (value unchanged). v10 recount equals read_share.

Project check of PR #570 (Brice Dudout): his decoder re-run (f. 370 97.3%, f. 373 99.7% of decoded letters align with the readings). View 420 fetched from openapi.bnf.fr and the bands of v25 and v29 read: v29 group 10 is a clear 8, not 9? (contrain-b-t, an enciphering slip), corrected in texts/f370_figures.txt; the second digit of the pape code at v25 looks like a 5 (code 25 rather than 23), r06 not re-read, code name left as 23. Read shares unchanged.

outcome.method_basis: The content of both letters comes from contemporary clear copies in fonds Brienne 13 (BnF NAF 6984), located through the Harlay piece numbers and Berger de Xivrey; Tomokiyo's published key for Maisse's Cipher (1592) was applied to the 81 transcribed characters of f. 370, which match the Brienne copy.
outcome.fraction_read_source: r2l 23 Oct 2026: both cipher passages transcribed group by group and aligned with their Brienne 13 copies: f. 370 2,293 groups (r2f, texts/f370_figures.txt), f. 373 3,958 groups (texts/f373_figures.txt, 36 of them doubtful on the image and carried by the copy), 6,251 in all; unread: group 90 (f. 370r l. 1, once). 6,250 / 6,251 = 0.999 of the visible cipher groups. The f. 370v line ends hidden in the gutter (about 147 copy letters) are read from the copy. Earlier: 0.99 (r2f, f. 373 estimated), 0.98 (v3), 0.87 (b29), 0.06 (reading audit 22 Oct), 1.0 withdrawn.
outcome.notes: Both letters read: the cipher of f. 370 and of f. 373 transcribed group by group and aligned with the contemporary Brienne 13 copies (97.6% and 97.8% letter agreement; the readings follow the figures where they differ). Key extended 23 Oct 2026 from the alignment: 71 = rr, 73 = tt (key1.tsv had uu), codes 23 = pape, 24 = Roy d'Espagne, 48 = ambassadeur, 49 = guerre. Split 14 Oct 2026: ff. 406 and 410, in a different cipher, are maisse1593.

reading_review.note: r2f 23 Oct 2026: the figures of f. 370r-v transcribed group by group from openapi.bnf.fr views 419-420 (texts/f370_figures.txt, 2,293 figure groups measured), decoded with Tomokiyo's key and aligned letter by letter with the Brienne 13 fol. 102v-103v copy (texts/f370_figures_vs_copy.md, research/reading_audit/r2f_align370.py): 2,255 of the 2,310 copy letters the figures cover agree (97.6%); 147 copy letters lie in the binding gutter of f. 370v (copy only). The reading now follows the figures where they differ in wording (vouldriez, ou restraigniez, concernans, traictees, lesquelz, si c'estoit) or spelling, keeps the copy over evident enciphering slips, and the copy's four doubtful words are settled (convier, veoir, verrons confirmed; vengez). v2_score: 0.979 plain (46/47), 1.0 explicit holes. Look-alike alternates: 0 letters of the reading rest on them (the 7/17 quelques at r02 is left with the copy).

texts.summary: Henri IV to Maisse, his ambassador at Venice: Cardinal de Gondi has passed near Venice and the marquis de Pisany follows him to the Pope for the Catholic royalists, so Maisse must stay at his post; Lambert returns to the Levant with the despatch for Brèves, which Maisse may amend; the King approves Maisse's warnings to the English ambassador and Brèves; the King of Spain's ambition; Lesdiguières's war in Piedmont and the help the Italian friends should give; the Pope's resolutions are awaited. The whole cipher passage is transcribed group by group and aligned with the contemporary Brienne 13 copy (97.6% letter agreement).

texts.label: f. 373, 7 Nov 1592 (figures of the whole cipher transcribed and aligned with the Brienne 13 fol. 104v-106v clear copy)
texts.summary: Henri IV acknowledges Maisse's letter of 4 October and will wait for the outcome of the Gondi and Pisany mission; urges the Venetian friends to help him with money and to work on the Pope, since only his person can preserve the Crown; approves Maisse's handling of the third-party (tiers parti) rumour; the duc de Retz has left without funding the Swiss, the League expects reinforcements while Parma is ill; Lesdiguières must be supported in Piedmont; Brèves has the Levant charge and Maisse is asked to stay at Venice a little longer. A clear postscript announces Joyeuse's defeat and death before Villemur.

reading_review.note: r2l 23 Oct 2026: the whole cipher of f. 373r-v transcribed group by group from the full-size Gallica views 422-423 (texts/f373_figures.txt, 3,958 groups in 66 lines, 36 doubtful, 3 struck; line spec f373_figures_spec.txt) and aligned letter by letter with the Brienne 13 fol. 104v-106v copy by research/reading_audit/r2l_align373.py (texts/f373_figures_vs_copy.md): 3,972 of the 4,062 copy letters of the cipher passage agree (97.8%), 29 substituted, 48 missing from the figures, 13 in code 24 (Roy d'Espagne). The reading now follows the figures where they differ in wording (vous pouvez tascher de, fort bon, asseurer ce faisant, Verac sa partialite, combien qui, par faulte d'estre, le moien que j'ay) and spelling. The figures were read line by line against the enciphered copy, so agreement is partly by construction; the 77 differences are what the image shows. v2_score 0.913 plain, 0.957 explicit holes. Earlier: b29 read from the copy, checked at five places; r2f Verac, charmez, sainement. Independent check (sr, 23 Oct 2026, texts/f373_sr_blind.txt): 6 lines drawn with random.seed(373) (r07, r15, r17, r18, r48, v13; 366 groups) transcribed blind from openapi.bnf.fr views 422-423 at full size, without f373_figures.txt or the enciphered copy: 342 groups agree, 94.1% (Dice, 366 vs 361 groups); per line 84.7-97.6%. The differences checked on re-crop (v13 'par deca que vous', r48 'aduiserez', r15 'faire', r18 'pourueu') are the blind reader's misses or crop-overlap repeats, the figures file is right where checked; so the 97.8% agreement with the copy is not only by construction. Grade A kept.
